utterances.text: And when you said that Mitar Vasiljevic believed what he was told, did he actually say that or did he make a different response when he was told that there was no one in the attic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG59
utterances.text: He said that he believed that there was no one there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did he also say that he trusted all of you because he knew you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG59
utterances.text: No, he didn't say anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: In answer to a question from the Prosecution, you said that he was not aggressive.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG59
utterances.text: He was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did he give orders to anyone or did he prohibit anyone from doing anything or did he do anything at all like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG59
utterances.text: No, he didn't do anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Could you tell us, if you can, what your impression was? Did he trust you and were there any problems along those lines? Did he indicate in any way anything other than that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG59
utterances.text: My opinion was that he trusted us, and he did not say anything to the people in the room and everyone believed him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Let me now refer to the so-called third incident. You described it as such. And That was the occasion when you and your brother were arrested and taken away. Who took part in this apart from the person who you referred to under the nickname Crnogorac or Montenegrin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG59
utterances.text: Milan Lukic, Rados Lukic, whom I knew, and this Crnogorac and a young man of some 22 or 23 years of age who ordered us to lay down this scarf and to put jewellery and money on this scarf.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So these persons took you to the Vilina Vlas Hotel; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG59
utterances.text: Crnogorac, the man called Crnogorac took us out of the house, and Milan Lukic and Rados were sitting in the car. Rados was driving, and the two of us were in the back.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Among the people you later saw in Vilina Vlas, did you know any of those people or did you recognise any of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG59
utterances.text: Do you mean the staff or do you mean the detainees?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, I'm not referring to the detainees, because you've already given us their names, but generally, anyone. The staff members or anyone else you may have seen there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG59
utterances.text: No, I didn't see anyone. There was no one at the reception desk.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I meant anyone, one of the guards or anyone else that you may have seen during the two days that you spent there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG59
utterances.text: I couldn't see anyone when I was locked up.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I have no further questions, but I would like to ask for the Prosecution's consent regarding what the witness says, that in his statement for the investigator he had said that Mitar had said that they were looking for an Avdo, who was looking for a Serb woman, to confirm that that does not exist in that statement. And no mention is made of Avdo or the killing of a Serb woman. All he said regarding Mitar was that he had asked whether there was anyone in the attic. So could we have their consent to avoid tendering the statement into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Ossogo?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is the Defence referring to the statement of the 13th of May, 2000?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is there more than one?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, simply be certain which document we are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Ossogo. I'm referring to the statement of the 13th of May, 2000. I have no other.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. We don't have any other statements either. Mr. President, we have a confrontation of two. I come from a civil law system. The witness is not absolutely bound by statements taken before. He may remember certain details later on, and he may convey it to the Judges this additional information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: May I interrupt you. It's not a question of anybody being bound. What will happen is that Mr. Domazet will suggest to us that this is something which the witness has made up. Whether we accept that submission or not is a different matter, but the question is relevant to the weight to be given to that piece of his evidence that he had not said so to the investigator. There may be all sorts of reasons why he didn't, and indeed you would be entitled to ask him in re-examination why he didn't or why he said it for the first time here, if you wish to, but this is the system that we have found works very much better than having volumes of statements in evidence. So if you accept that -- do you accept that it is not stated in his statement of the 13th of May, 2000?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Do you want to ask him any questions in re-examination about that or about anything else?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, absolutely not, Mr. President. We didn't ask any questions about this particular aspect, which was not important for us. It was a question of obtaining certain information regarding mass treatment and persecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Ossogo, I'm not asking you to explain it. I merely said you may, if you wish, ask the witness why he raised it for the first time here and had not said anything about it to the investigator. That was not something that was put to the witness in cross-examination, so you are entitled to put it if you wish, but I don't want you giving evidence from the bar table as to why it wasn't asked of him at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand. I understand, Mr. President. We agree with Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. Now, do you want to ask the witness any questions in re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, just two observations.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] VG59, when Mitar Vasiljevic was standing at the door, armed with a weapon, were you free, you and all the others in the room, were you free to move about? Could you come and go as you wished?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG59
utterances.text: No. We could not leave the house. We had to sit down there. We had to remain seated.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: You were obliged to be seated because he was bearing a weapon and prevented you from going out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG59
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: You also --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG59
utterances.text: He told us to sit down.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: I see. You also said, concerning the second incident, that when the group came back with Milan at its head, you did not notice Mitar Vasiljevic; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG59
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: But he might have been in that group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG59
utterances.text: I assume so.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: And regarding the third incident, when you were taken to the Vilina Vlas Hotel, you didn't see him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG59
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: You are indicating his presence only when you actually saw him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG59
utterances.text: I only saw him in the first incident, and I assume that he was there during the second incident because he was a member of that group called Eagles. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes. Judge Taya would like to ask a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TAYA
utterances.text: VG59, can you remember the approximate date and month when the third incident occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG59
utterances.text: The third incident could have taken place at the beginning of June. I cannot remember the exact date. I assume it was the 4th or 5th of June. It could have been.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TAYA
utterances.text: At the time of the third incident, do you presume that Mitar Vasiljevic participated in the third incident? If not, what is the reason why you presume differently from the second incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG59
utterances.text: I presume that he was in the third incident, too, in view of the fact that I didn't see him. But when my brother and I were taken out, it was already dark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, do you want to ask any questions arising out of those questions of Judge Taya?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would have a question, Your Honour, in this connection and also in connection, if I may, what Mr. Ossogo mentioned in his re-examination, and that is the following --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Wait a minute. The re-examination is a different question. Is there anything arising out of Judge Taya's questions, by all means, so ask those first, would you?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As regards the third incident, you clearly told us who were the participants and who was with you in the car; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG59
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You also said that in Vilina Vlas, you didn't see any person that you knew.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG59
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: How then can I interpret your recent answer to the effect that you assume that Mitar Vasiljevic was involved in the third incident? Was it again because he was there during the first incident, so on the basis of that you presume he was a member of the group, or is there any other reason?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG59
utterances.text: Because in the first incident, he was a member of the Eagles together with Milan Lukic, and that is why I presume that he could have been in the third incident as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Even though you did not see him at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG59
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Domazet, if I may suggest, you have in fact covered the same ground anyway, quite legitimately, but you covered the same ground that the re-examination had. Is there anything else you want to ask arising out of the re-examination? The evidence that he has given is very clear. He saw him only on the first occasion. He drew the inference I think is probably the most accurate way of saying it, he drew the inference that he was there on the second and third occasion because he understood him to be a member of the White Eagles. That's the evidence. You can challenge it as you wish, but that's what he has said, and he's said it now, I think, three times.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, but in connection with the question of Mr. Ossogo and the explanation given by the witness at the time differs somewhat from his answer to my question, and that is in answer to my question as to whether Mitar Vasiljevic gave any orders or any prohibitions or said anything like that, the witness said no. And now in answer to a direct question from Mr. Ossogo, he said that no one could go out because those were the orders allegedly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If he was standing at the door in the role of guard, it's quite logical that we couldn't leave the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So because he was in the doorway carrying a weapon, you assumed that no one could go out, but no such order was given by him, if I understood you correctly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG59
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Domazet, the statement in the re-examination that you are referring to was simply this answer: "He told us to sit down." That's all. Now, I think we can take it we've got the final version from what the witness has now said, and I don't really see there's any point in challenging that unless you can persuade us to the contrary.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, sir, thank you very much for coming here to give evidence and for the evidence which you've given. You are now free to leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, whilst the next witness is coming, may I ask you a question? It arises out of Mr. Poljo's evidence. I assume that we will be asked to draw the inference that because the flow of the river was downstream from Visegrad that these bodies did come from Visegrad, but is there anywhere higher up the river or in between Visegrad and where he was living from which the bodies could have come? Are there dams across the river at any stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, there will be a witness testifying next week that will be able to testify to facts regarding this. I would say that the dam, the Visegrad dam that you've heard a great deal about, is further south of Visegrad. So Visegrad lies between the dam and Slap.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. Because we've got no other means, unless there is something from the material taken from the bodies that identified them as having come specifically from Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, there will be some testimony next week regarding some of the bodies that were able to be identified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I just thought I'd raise it. Now, who is your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, before we call the next witness, I ask that we return to the earlier discussion regarding the experts. Mr. Domazet and I have had a conversation regarding that. I'd like to inform the Court of the progress. Regarding Mr. John Clark, who is scheduled to testify next Tuesday, Mr. Domazet has agreed to waive his right to have Mr. Clark's report for 21 days and will be prepared to cross-examine him next Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Ms. Ewa Tabeau who was schedule to testify this afternoon, Mr. Domazet will agree to cross-examine her tomorrow, and we will call her tomorrow. The one that Mr. Domazet would like his full 21 days to evaluate the report is Dr. de Grave, who was scheduled to testify tomorrow. Over lunch, I will endeavour to speak with Dr. de Grave and find out the next available date that he is able to attend the Tribunal, and I will report that to the Court this afternoon so that we can schedule his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Has there been a fifth version of this week's schedule.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: There soon will be another version, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But there was no sign on this one of Ms. Tabeau, that's all. The most recent one that I have, there is no reference to Ms. Tabeau, unless she has a pseudonym which I don't believe she would have.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the one that I refer the Court to is this one that I presented Monday which had the entire trial schedule, the anticipated trial schedule on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I thought this one was meant to be the last word, the one which has just this week day by day.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: As Your Honour is aware, some of the problems we've had getting witnesses up here, this schedule seems to change on an hourly basis. But the one that I presented to the Court that had the entire trial schedule is the one I believe is the most accurate although it will change after some of the events of today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We would like the weekly one though with the protective measures. You don't need to do it quite as elaborately as you have here, but it would be a help to have that. All right. Well, then, have you got enough witnesses for us to proceed today?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: There are two more witnesses that are scheduled for today. I also want to advise the Court that Mr. Tokaca who was schedule for Thursday and who I spoke to last night and was all ready to fly today, there's been some problem. I'm not fully aware of the circumstances of the problem, but he will not be here for Thursday. I again will try to find out the details of what happened. I'm led to believe it was some problem with a visa, and I will advise the Court this afternoon as to the earliest time we might expect Mr. Tokaca.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think I can say quite safely that we do understand the problems that you have of getting the witnesses here and of obtaining all the necessary visas for them and provided that you have got some back-up somewhere along the line, perhaps bringing in a few more witnesses in case there are problems for the following week, we will fit in with how you can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, so the Court is aware, we have endeavoured to bring every witness to the Tribunal as soon as possible, and it's only the visa problems that are delaying them at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: What do you foresee then being the rest of the week? I suppose you may have to wait to see whether Dr. de Grave, for example, is available on Thursday.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I will check with him on the lunch break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And so that we can notify those who are the important people who provide the interpreters, the court reporters, the rest of the court staff, we will have to know about Friday as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, when I return from lunch, I will have our best estimate of the remainder of the week and the week after, if that's acceptable to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, now, have you got the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, the next witness is outside. Before I would do that I would like to, at this time, tender the agreed facts about to be presented to the Chamber. It is Prosecution number 36.1, are the agreed facts in English, and bear the signatures of both myself and Mr. Domazet. And Exhibit 36.2 are the agreed facts in the Serbian language and bears the signature of the accused, Mr. Domazet, and myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Perhaps you'll have to do a small translation for us, but the word "stipulate," as I've already drawn your attention to, means different things to different people. I realise in America that it is something that is used, I think to say, admit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Or an agreed fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: For example, in 3(A), it's not necessary to prove that it was international in this case, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, but Mr. Domazet felt strongly to add that qualification into it, and the Prosecution agreed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The copies that I have have Mr. Domazet's signature on the English and Mr. Domazet's and Mr. Vasiljevic's on the B/C/S. So far, your signature does not appear on either of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, those copies were made before I signed them. The actual two exhibits which will be tendered into evidence I have here, and have my signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, we'll give you these back. This is a completely new document you're giving us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: This is the same document with my signature on it that we will be tendering into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is it the English or the B/C/S version?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm tendering both of them, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, then, those will be the only documents we need, won't they? Well, have they not got the other signatures on them?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: These have all the signatures on them now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: All right. Give those ones back. We'll take those as the exhibits. Have you only the one copy of each?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's All right. They can be copied. They will be Exhibits P36.1 and 36.2.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. The Serbian language one being P36.2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: All right. Now, can we have the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The Prosecution would call VG77.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The pseudonym sheet will be Exhibit P78, and it will be under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now, madam, will you please make the statutory -- the solemn declaration in the document which the court usher is showing you. You have to read it out, madam. Are you all right to go ahead?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you, madam. Sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Do you feel ready to go ahead?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Groome

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Witness 77, I would ask you to look at Prosecution 78 and read that document. Is that your name on the top of that document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And is that your date of birth on that document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And is that your current address on that document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask you, if you have to refer to the person listed on that document, I would ask that you use the pseudonym VG87.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you born in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And have you lived most of your life in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were you married?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And do you have children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: I do, two.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to draw your attention to the spring of 1992. Did there come a time during April of that year that you left Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes, in June. On the 18th -- 17th or 18th of June. I don't know for sure. I think it was the 18th.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to draw your attention to a time earlier than that. Was there a time that you left briefly for a village called Medjedja?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And when was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: I can't remember whether it was in April. In April.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was that at the same time that many people left Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you return from that village to Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: We did return.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And soon after returning, was your husband arrested?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Without telling us the actual address, would you tell us what street in Visegrad you lived on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And the area in which you lived, was that a predominantly Muslim area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Predominantly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you returned to Visegrad, did you return to your home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was there ever a time that you hid in the woods during the spring of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes. Quite frequently, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And would these be the woods close to where you lived on [redacted]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes, called Babin Potok.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was there ever a time that you were harassed as you passed by the Visegradska Banja during this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. When I went from Babin Potok to the village of Dubovo, where my husband is from, and then when I went back to Visegrad, we were mistreated. They yelled at us, saying we should be killed, forced into the river. They forced us to sit down, to get up, and then they mistreated us all the way to my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you go to your house? Did you go into your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes. I got to my house. I entered inside. They followed us. They searched us. They asked where my children were, my husband. They found my money. They took my money away, and they left.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And how long did you remain in your house at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: I was there for 15 days when I returned to the village from my house in [redacted], though I didn't spend all the nights in my own house. I spent some of them at my neighbour's.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: [redacted] are you familiar with two houses belonging to a family by the name of Memic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes, do I know that, because it's close to my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And are those two houses directly on [redacted]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: It is [redacted] all the way from my house and further up.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the school on [redacted]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And where are the Memic houses in relation to the school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: When you're going uphill on the left-hand side. If you're going up along [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that they are across from the school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes, across from the school. You're quite right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are you familiar with a house belonging to Adem Omeragic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: I am, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And where is that house in relation to the Memic houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: It is on the left-hand side of Jusuf and Mujo Memic's house, next to the creek.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How far away is the Omeragic house from this creek?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but right close to the creek. It's not a big stream. It's like a small valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time in the spring of 1992 that a person by the name of Lukic came and spoke with you and a friend of yours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you approximate to the Court when this was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: It was in June.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you describe for the Court what you remember about this person named Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: I remember, when I was at my neighbour's, Ibrahim Memic's house, Milan Lukic came and another man, and I can't remember his name. They took down our names, mine, Ibrahim Memic, his mother, wife, daughters-in-law, telling us that we mustn't go anywhere, that we were safe there, and that they would come and fetch us and take us to safety.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think you're court manager should have as his first task to remind the Prosecution counsel that we are due to adjourn. I know that it's difficult, but nevertheless, we have got certain obligations to the interpreting and court reporting staff. We will adjourn now until 2.30. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, before I resume, I have provided the court deputy with an updated schedule of where the situation stands now. At some point that's convenient for the Court, perhaps we can discuss it later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It would be a good idea if these things are dated and if there's more than one on one day, we can have the date with a 1 or 2 after it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at the top line I have today's date and 2.00 being the last time it was updated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Oh, that's very good. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Witness VG77, before we took our break, you were describing an event that took occurred in of a friend of yours' house in which Milan Lukic was present. Do you recall what you were testifying about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would you tell us again what exactly these people said to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: These people told us that we shouldn't leave the place until they came because it wasn't safe and that they would come and -- and take us to some safe place.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did both men speak to you or did just one of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Both. Both men spoke to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were you able to tell from -- the person you're identifying as Milan Lukic, I'd ask you to describe his physical appearance for the Court.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: He was wearing a uniform, and the other one, I couldn't remember what he was wearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And the uniform that Mr. Lukic was wearing, did it have any insignias on it or any lettering that you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: No. I can't remember. The only thing that I remember was that he was wearing a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The other person, when he spoke, was there anything unique about his voice that you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Well, one of the daughters of -- daughter of the owner was asked her -- asked the woman whether she was there, and she said that they had gone to school together, that they were in school together.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you take that to mean that he was from Visegrad as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Approximately what time of the day was this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: I can't remember whether it was -- in the afternoon or around about noon, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, a couple of days later, did you see a group of people from the village of Koritnik on Pionirska street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And as best you remember, how many days were between this first incident with Milan Lukic and this sighting of people from Koritnik on Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Two days had passed perhaps. Between two and three days. Not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What was your best recollection of what day this was when you saw the people from Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: I can't remember the day. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, where were you when you saw these people from Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: I was at home. I called one of my neighbours and asked him whether I was safe to remain at home and whether he could help me. He said he -- I could not go, that I should stay there because it was not safe. Then I left with my grandfather and grandmother as well, and we left, and we walked about 100 metres. And I went to Mujo Memic's house, and I met those people from Koritnik. I met a group. I don't know how many there were in that group. Well, I was -- I first noticed a baby --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The group that you saw from Koritnik, could you tell which direction they were coming from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Up from Pionirska, from the main street to Pionirska.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that they were coming away from the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: They were coming from their village. I stood with them. They asked me where I was going. I said I was going to Drina, to a neighbour, to his house. And then they said, "How come you are leaving this place?" They told us that there were many empty houses there and that we should find accommodations in Mahala and Pionirska Street. I said, was told that the houses were empty and that we were amongst the last and that we would be leaving.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You mentioned a baby among this group of people. Approximately how old was that baby?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I talked is to these people. I knew these people. I asked -- I wondered if we had done something wrong to someone. Why was the baby to blame? And I told the mother of the child, "Where are you going with that baby? How old is that baby?" She told me, "Two days old. I gave birth to her in a forest in Paocina two days previously."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, where precisely on Pironirska Street was this group people from Koritnik when you first saw them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: That group was at Mujo Memic's home. Number 87 it was. By number 87.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And for approximately how long did you stop and speak with these people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Well, about five or six minutes, perhaps ten minutes we stood there. At the most, ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did any of the people in this group tell you where they were going?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: They asked me whether they could go into those houses. I said all those houses were empty. "You can go into those houses. You can go into my house. It's empty." They stood in their tracks because they were not aware of what had been going on there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: These people, were they carrying any bags with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes. They were carrying travelling bags, blankets, wardrobe over those bags.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did anyone from this group tell you that they were instructed by Serbs to come to this part of town and to occupy those houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes. They were told by the Serbs, as neighbours, that they had to leave these places, that they were not safe in that village, that they had to go into the city, and that they should find accommodations in Pironirska Street because there were plenty of empty houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you left this group of people and continued on your way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you continue to walk down Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes. I went down Pionirska Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you walking in the direction of the centre of town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes, towards the centre of town.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: After you met this group of people, did you meet anyone else on the street that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: I met, as I was leaving Pionirska Street, in the direction of the petrol pump, I met Mitar Vasiljevic and another soldier who was with him. They stopped us there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to describe the person you're referring to as Mitar Vasiljevic as best you can remember.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Well, I remembered the hat he wore on his head.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe it for us, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Well, he walked towards us. He stopped us there, my grandmother, grandfather, and they were asking us where we were going. I said that we were going to the Drina, to a neighbour, and he said, "You cannot pass there." And he asked me where I was going, and I said that I was going to fetch my children from the Drina and take them home. And he told me, "You cannot pass. You're not safe after 3.00 p.m. If someone kills you, I will not be held responsible and no one will be held responsible." And to my grandfather, he also said that he should go and bury the dead that were laying around in those houses. "I can't do that," he said. "I have to go where my children are." He was persistent. He wanted to go back at all costs. I said that I had to go and fetch the children. And he kept calling, "Return. Return. There is no passage there." And there we stopped, as if we were going to go back. Then he went along Pironirska Street with the other soldier. Then we went behind them, then we stopped, and then we turned towards the centre of the city.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Witness 77, you've described two people. Who was the person who was speaking to you at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Mitar spoke to us. And the other person was standing next to him. He said, "Yes, yes. You go back."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When Mitar Vasiljevic told you to go back, what did you understand that to mean? Go back where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Well, I understood that we had to go back with the people from Koritnik, the people I had met 50 metres before. I don't -- I'm not quite sure. I thought that we had to go along with them, because I didn't know what would happen later on. I understood that he was making us go, return with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: During the time that he's speaking to you, does he ever refer to the group of people from Koritnik village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: No, he didn't mention that group of people. He only told us that if someone killed us after 3.00 p.m., that he would not be held responsible.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you go back, as you were instructed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: No, I didn't go back that day. That was in the afternoon when this happened, when he was trying to get us to go back. I went to Drina with my family. I spent the night there, and then I returned very early. It must have been very early, about 7.00 a.m. I don't know what day it was. I can't remember. Then when we came there to Pionirska street, near the house of Jusuf Memic, we saw that the house had burnt down. There was a thunder storm that night. There was a lot of shooting. We don't know whether it was the grenades or the shells or whether it was thunder. It was a disaster.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Witness 77, I want to ask you specific questions. I'd ask you, after you finish the specific answer, give me an opportunity to ask another question. I want to take you back to the time that you're having this conversation with Mr. Vasiljevic. Why did you not go back as you were instructed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Well, we didn't go back because there was no one there except for the people from Koritnik, because everyone had left and we didn't dare stay there any longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What did you say to this person you're referring to as Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Well, I told him that I was going for my children and then that I would come back.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was that the truth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: That was the truth. Of course it was the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where were your children at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Well, my children were in Austria at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time later in the day that you did return to your home on [redacted]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And approximately when that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Early in the morning when I said that I would return the children. I didn't go back, but early in the morning, at 7.00 a.m., I returned to [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And when you returned to [redacted], did you have an opportunity to go past the Memic house again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And would you describe for the Court what you observed about the condition of that house later in the day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Please describe it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Jusuf Memic's house had burnt down that night. When I came there with my neighbour, I saw that the roof had burnt down, that everything was falling down. And when I saw that the house was burning, we went to Mujo's house, and we wondered where the people from Koritnik were, where they had spent the night and what had happened to them. We looked around in -- we look at Omeragic's house. We saw that it was on fire. The smoke wag coming out of the windows. And then we wondered whether those people were there in that house. We were asking each other, and we were answering each other, and we said, "Yes. No." And then we went to Mujo's house and there we stopped. We didn't see anyone. We didn't hear anyone. Everything was devastated. It was all very quiet and sad. Then we went to number 87, the house in 87. We enter the house. We called out people. No one responded. We saw corridors full of bags which these people from Koritnik were carrying. This was one storey, on one floor. We called the owner. He wasn't there. Then we went to the first floor. We also called out. There was no one. There were bags there also in the corridors, in the rooms. We called out. No one responded.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Witness 77, when you returned to Pionirska Street, you mentioned seeing bags. Did you recognise these bags as the bags you saw in the possession of the people from Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you see any trace of the people from Koritnik there on Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: No, I didn't. There was no -- there were no traces, but we saw their clothes, their bags. The clothes were on their bags. The blankets were on the bags. I saw the people carrying those bags and those clothes and blankets and that they were in that house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And which houses did you see had been burnt down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Adem's house and Jusuf Memic's house. They were burnt down that night.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: By Adem's house are you referring to Adem Omeragic's house, by the creek?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, near the creek.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How close did you come to that house or did you go to that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: We didn't go to the house, but my neighbour and I had supposed that the people in that house had burnt down also, along with the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How long did you remain in the area of these two houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Well, we went up to Muja's house. There there was no one. [redacted] [redacted]. When I went into the house, everything was broken, was destroyed. Everything that could have been taken away was taken away. We walked out. We went to Jusuf Memic's stalls. He had cows there and we tried to let the cows loose so as to avoid having them being burnt. When we got to his stalls, the stalls, the barn had burnt down. The cows were not there, someone had let them loose, and the barn had already burnt down.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean by the condition having changed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: No. No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you're describing going to the stable which belonged to Jusuf Memic. Where is that stable with respect to the house belonging to Adem Omeragic by the creek?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Well, the stables of Jusuf Memic were perhaps 200, 300 metres from Adem Omeragic's place.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At that time, was the house -- was the roof on the house still intact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Jusuf Memic. You mean Adem's house or Jusuf's house?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Adem Omeragic's house by the creek.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: No. No. The roof -- well, we walked around there by Jusuf's stables. We looked at the smoke going out of Adem's house. This went on. And we stood there. Then we went to Hajra's house and there we watched from the window when the roof collapsed. It burnt and it collapsed. It fell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Normally.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, after this day, did there come a day when you left Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: That night, well, I spent in the neighbourhood at my neighbour Hajra's place. The lights were on the whole night. Of course, we didn't switch it off. Some people below were walking up and about. We didn't know who they were. They didn't mistreat us in any way. And that night, of course, we couldn't sleep. The next day, we went to Drina again, and there we spent some time with some other neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you leave Visegrad that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: We didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When did you leave Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Well, I left -- well, it was either the 17th or the 18th of June. I don't know exactly. Whether it was the 17th or the 18th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And approximately how many days transpired between the day that you saw Adem Omeragic's house by the creek burning and the day you left Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Well, perhaps the third day. We left there the third day, on the third day.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you've described a person or referred to a person by the name of Mitar Vasiljevic throughout your testimony. I would ask you to describe for the Court how you know this person.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Well, I used to know him even before. I didn't pay much attention to him, but I did know him. I did know him very well, but I would -- I saw him. I had seen him earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you describe for us where you saw him prior to the day that you've described here in court? Was there a particular place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: No. I had no contact with him ever. I met him a couple of times. Sometimes in town. I would meet him in town in the Mahala, at Cadza's, because I never paid much attention to him ever.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask you to look around the courtroom here today and tell us whether you recognise anybody here in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Well, I recognised him as soon as I walked in through the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The person who you're referring to now, would you describe where he is now in this courtroom and describe something that he's wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Well, the person is on the left-hand side. He has a white shirt, and he has a multicolored jacket.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, may the record reflect the witness has indicated the accused in this matter? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think you better ask her which row, because I see nobody with a multicolored jacket except one of the court reporters.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would you describe more precisely what row this person is sitting in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Behind, in the background.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe more precisely the colour of this person's jacket?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Well, yellowish. I can't see very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think we've got it. It can be stated that she has identified the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is this the person who instructed you to return back and to join the people from Koritnik on Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I'm going to ask that the witness -- or Exhibit P17.4 be placed in the ELMO. It is in the binders I have provided the Court and we also have the black and white copies if the Court would like.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that you take the black pen, the permanent marker, and I'm going to ask you to write -- on this table to your right there's this picture.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to write "VG77" on the bottom so that we know these markings were made by you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I would ask if the witness -- if it's not possible for the witness to draw on the ELMO, I would ask that we put the photograph in front of the witness and I will ask her to make some markings and then we will put it back on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to circle the house that you've describe as Jusuf Memic's house, and put the initials "JM" to indicate that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I would ask you to circle the house belonging to Adem Omeragic by the creek. Draw a circle around it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And would you put the letters "AO" inside that circle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I would ask you just to put the initial "P" to indicate which of the streets on that photograph is Pionirska Street. Put the letter "P".

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: I didn't understand what you have just said about the lettering, about the letters.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I would ask you just to put the letter "P" on the street you've referred to as Pionirska Street, to tell us which street is Pionirska Street.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: [In English] Yeah, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, I want you to draw a circle to indicate your best approximation of where Mitar Vasiljevic was at the time you had a conversation with him.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: How? With a letter or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Just a circle. Then I'll ask you to do the initials.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And would you put "MV" inside that circle to indicate where he was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The place that you're approximating, is it off that picture?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So have you drawn a circle to indicate where it was that you saw Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Those are all the markings I'm going to the witness to make. Your Honour, would it assist the Chamber to indicate all the markings she's made now? I don't believe her last marking is visible on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's where she saw the accused?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now it's visible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, when you said today and also in your earlier statement the place where you saw two men whom you identified as Mitar Vasiljevic and another soldier you said that this was at the end or at the beginning of Pionirska Street, depending on the direction, at the crossroads with the road leading to the petrol station. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: That road which leads to the petrol station, is that the road leading towards the village of Jagodina or Uzice? That is the main road.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes, the main road for Uzice and Pionirska Street branches off of it to the left and that's where Vasiljevic was standing with the soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So he was standing there with this other person on the corner of this road leading from Visegrad to Uzice, and that is also the beginning of Pionirska Street; is it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: The spot that you have marked on this photograph is at the bottom of this photograph, but that is not the intersection with the road you have just told us about, which in my view is much, much further away than that this. So could you look at this photograph once again and see whether the spot that you have described is visible on this photograph or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: No. The intersection cannot be seen on this photograph at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You can see the school well, with the school yard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: The intersection at which you saw Mitar Vasiljevic is quite a bit further away along the Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And it is not visible on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: It is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Does that mean that you are correcting the marking that you made on this photograph, the circle indicating the spot where Mitar Vasiljevic was standing? Because he seems to be between two houses, which is not that spot.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: He was standing near this house. We were going towards each other, and this man with him had a limp in one leg, this man who was standing at the entrance to that house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So you saw him at the intersection of Pionirska Street and the road leading to Uzice, towards the petrol station going out of Visegrad towards Uzice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: He entered Pionirska Street from the road leading to Uzice, so he turned into Pionirska Street, that intersection, and he was moving from that intersection along Pionirska Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I understood that, but that intersection is not shown on this photograph, is it? Could you tell me, this other road leading to the petrol station and leading out of Visegrad, how far away is it from the school in Pionirska Street? Roughly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: I can't. I never measured the distance, but it's not far. You go up Pionirska Street. I don't know whether it's 200 or 250 metres as you walk up Pionirska Street. I don't know, I never measured it, but it's not far.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I have to go back to this photograph yet again, which does not show this road or, rather, the intersection. Do you still maintain that the spot where you saw Mitar Vasiljevic can be seen on this photograph or is it a spot in Pionirska Street but a part of the street which is not shown on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: As far as I can see here, I don't see it. Maybe it was -- the photograph was taken in two parts and then attached. As far as I can see, the intersection is not visible. I see the Memic house, his son's house, and the house number 87. I see Momo's house, Momo and Mimo. I see Gusa's house that had a bakery. I see Jusuf Memic's house. Those houses I can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. You described the person as a person wearing a big straw hat. Do you remember anything else that this person was wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: No, I cannot remember that day. I remember most this hat, this straw hat, big straw hat that he was wearing. And I was confused when I met him, when he said that we had to go back, and after that, I couldn't see anything any more. I was so upset.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Talking about this hat, you said it was a straw hat. Do you remember its colour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yellow, as far as I can remember. It was a yellow hat.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You said that he was telling you to turn back. At the same time, did he mention at all this group from Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: No. He said that we should go back together with the people, that no one could guarantee our safety after 3.00, and that he wouldn't be held responsible for our safety.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And this other person who was there, who you described today as a soldier, because in your statement with the investigator, you described him as a Serb. What is the difference? At the time you didn't say he was a soldier, but today you're saying he was a soldier.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: This other one was a soldier, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: How was he dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: He was wearing a uniform, a military uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know a person called [redacted] madam?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you see [redacted] anywhere that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So you didn't see him that day in Pionirska Street, nor with Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: No. [redacted] lived in Crnic, on the other bank of the Drina, across the Drina River.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you know a person with the same name and surname who lived in Sase?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Sase. What name did you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [redacted].

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you were leaving your house in [redacted] that day and when you came across this group of people, was anyone else in those houses, apart from you, from among the people who used to live in those houses that you knew?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: You mean whether anyone stayed behind after we had left that last day?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: The day you met the group from Koritnik, do you remember whether anyone else had stayed in their houses or was there no one left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: As far as I know, [redacted] wife had stayed behind, another tenant, and they lived in the same house. Whether their daughter or daughter-in-law or grandchild was there, a child of two or three, as far as I know, they were there when I left and when we met Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Those are the only persons that you knew had stayed behind when you left and walked up Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do those people live above or below the Memics' house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Above the Mujo Memic's house. It was the house above Mujo Memic's. That is where they lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: At the time, did you see a person that I have to refer to as -- with her initials, VG115, so could the witness be shown the name and surname of this witness for her to be able to answer my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You see the highlighted name against the number?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Was that person on that day in Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: This person was in Visegrad for two years afterwards, for two years, this person.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: My question was whether you saw her then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: I did not see her, but I know that she was there. She lived near

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So according to you, she lived there for another two nears in

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes. Let me try and explain. It's about 250 or 300 metres again, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Are you familiar with that house? You know it well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Is it possible to see the Memic house from that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: I don't know. I doubt it. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And what about the Omeragic house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: No. It cannot be seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You're quite about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: I'm quite sure, because there are other houses in between that obstruct the view to the Omeragic house which was next to the creek.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You said, madam, that you knew of this witness, VG115, that she lived in Visegrad for another two years.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: How do you know that, since as far as I know, you have left. You left Visegrad in June 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: I know because her husband, I can't give you the name --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, don't.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Her husband was where I was and one child was with him. The boy and the girl was with her mother. Then they met when it was possible to leave. After maybe four years, they got together again, she and her husband.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When did you hear that Mitar Vasiljevic was arrested? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: I can't remember, but I heard immediately when they announced it on the news on television that he had been arrested.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you see the film of his arrest?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you, I'm not that interested in politics. When I switch it on, if that subject is featured, I watch. I'm not a politician to be following the situation in any detail, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I didn't think that you were involved in politics. I was just wondering whether you watched those features from The Hague, news reports. Did you see the detailed report of his arrival in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes, I did see it on television. I saw it once. I saw him once here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you remember how many times you made statements in connection with this case? Did you give statements to the investigator of the Prosecution on this case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Twice and never again except for this time now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Were you shown a photograph spread showing various people for you to identify Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you recognise him on the photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: I did not, because photographs are not the same as real life. I cannot recognise people on a photograph in the same way I do when I meet them, because the pictures are magnified. So you can't recognise him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So on those photographs, you did not recognise Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: May I ask you, how did it come about for you to give a statement? How did they learn about you as a witness? Did you notify them yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: I don't know at all who gave my name as a possible witness, because what do I know? There were always stories about what people had lived through. People were talking about that. And there is a person in Visegrad, and she will be coming here, and maybe she told these people that I had lived through this and that I had seen these things linked to Mitar, and maybe she informed them that I knew about him and that is why they called me, and I went and made a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you remember the occasion when you saw Mitar Vasiljevic on television, if that was only once, as you said? Was this before you gave your statement to the investigator or afterwards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Afterwards. No. Just a moment, please. Once I saw him once before, and once afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So you saw him twice on television, once before you made your statement and one afterwards.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: I made a statement once when I was invited to do so, and after that I saw him on television. And then I made a statement for the second time, and then they invited me to come here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: In addition to this identification, if I am not wrong, I think in your statement you said yourself that you would not be able to recognise him from a photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: At the time, I could not recognise him, but today, as I walked through the door, I felt sick as soon as I saw him. You probably noticed. I suddenly remembered his image when I met him in Visegrad, and I remembered that scene and this depression, and I felt unwell. I recognised him immediately here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Very well. You will admit that it wasn't difficult to recognise him in here, but did he differ in any way from the person you saw some nine years ago compared to what he looks like now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. He was wearing a hat then. But still today, this face I recognised it as soon as I walked through the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Madam, you said that you left [redacted] that afternoon because you were afraid as many people had abandoned the area, almost all of them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes, all the neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: But you went back the next morning nevertheless?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Weren't you afraid to go back the next morning or was it just in the night that you were afraid?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: I didn't think. I never gave it a thought. I expected to be killed any moment, to be hit by a bullet, to be picked up and detained. So I never gave a thought to my safety because the power was in their hands. They did what they wanted.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When this group you that you identified as the group from Koritnik near the Memic house, you said you couldn't tell how many they were, but can you tell us approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: I can't tell when I don't know the exact number. I can tell you it was quite a decent group. How many people, I don't know, but quite a number.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Something else linked to the recognition of the person you saw on the corner of this street. You claim that this was a person who you came across a couple of times in town.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I would like to know, how could you tell that this person you met a couple of times in town and that you saw on the corner of Pionirska Street and this other road, how did you know that his name was Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: My father-in-law was with me, and he knew him, but he didn't dare say to him, "Neighbour Mitar, let us pass," which was quite normal. May I ask a question?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Not to me, but if Their Honours allow it, that's another matter. It is my duty to ask questions here and yours to answer for the moment. So if Their Honours allow it, please go ahead?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is it something that you don't understand, madam, or is it just a matter of curiosity that you want to ask the question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: No, not out of curiosity, but I want to say a couple of words more about Mitar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Domazet, the Prosecution would be able to ask her what she wanted to ask. My suggestion to you is that it would be better for you to hear it so that you can cross-examine on it if necessary. I'm not trying to force you into it. I'm just suggesting to you that it may be to your benefit to have what she wants to say said now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Actually, I have just completed my cross-examination. If the Prosecution has anything else to ask, it's up to them, but I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Groome, if you want to ask, it would be new matter upon which there can be cross-examination. I think that's clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think if the witness wants to say anything, let's hear what it is. If it turns out to be irrelevant, we can ignore it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Witness VG77, what is this additional information you want to tell us about Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG77
utterances.text: I wanted to say that the last day, the 17th or the 18th -- I think it was the 18th of June, when they told us that there would be a convey a 8.00, and we started out, I spent the last night at my neighbour's, also in [redacted], we met Mitar near an auto part shop, a shop selling parts for automobiles. He met us. He was carrying a hand grenade. He was carrying an automatic rifle. He provoked us there. He forced us to sit down, to get up, sit down, get up. This neighbour was pushing his old mother who was blind, in a wheelchair, and he was saying, "Where are you taking that excrement? Throw it into the Drina." He wanted to kill us. He waved the hand grenade at us to kill us all. He mistreated us. Then he forced us to go in front of the SUP. We got in front of the SUP. He still had his weapon in his hand. Then three men came out of the SUP, down the steps, and asked him, "Mitar, where are you chasing those people to?" And he said, "I want to kill them." They said to him, "Leave" -- "let the people be. There's a convoy at 8.00." He said, "They should be killed." And they said to him, "Leave the people alone. There's a convey for them at 8.00 to take them to Olovo." And we lined up two by two. We held hands. We were to go along the Drina River, and that is how they let us go. We got to the square, and that day we left. That was the last day.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did these people --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Just one moment. Just one moment. Are you able to tell me, Mr. Groome, whether any of this was in her statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It was not, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, I think that raises an issue which we had better discuss in the absence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: We'll excuse her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Madam, we want to discuss that material you've just given us, and we'll have to do it when you are out of court. So if you would go with the usher for a few moments, we'll let you back into court shortly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, it produces a problem. We'll have to hear what Mr. Domazet wants to say about it, but if none of that was in the statement, there are problems with us taking any account of it, where the Defence has had no warning that it's going to be given.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution had no warning that she was going to introduce that. Obviously we didn't ask any questions regarding that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm not trying to assign blame, I'm trying to work out what we can do with it. She had to say it, but what can we do with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
