utterances.text: Your Honour, it would be the Prosecution position that if a witness, during the course of their testimony recalls additional information, the mere fact that it wasn't contained in their original statement shouldn't be a legal bar to the Court listening to that evidence. Of course, the Court -- Mr. Domazet is free to argue the credibility of that additional information and the Court is free to weigh it as it sees fit, but I don't think there should be any legal bar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It depends, does it not, upon the nature of the additional material? If it is material of this type, my own view would be that the Defence must be given fair warning of it and, if necessary, the opportunity to consider it, to investigate it, and then to answer it. If this had just been some minor matter, I would agree with you that most counsel for an accused would be able to take it in their stride. But this is hardly that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: May I suggest the following then, Your Honour? That we conclude with this witness today, and if Mr. Domazet does seek to do some additional investigation, we can make arrangements for this witness to be recalled at a later time for additional cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. That seems a reasonable thing. Well, Mr. Domazet, I would not expect you to be able to stand up and cross-examine her at this stage. Obviously, you will have some sort of an argument as to the credit to be given to it because it was not in the statement, but it is of some importance. What do you suggest that we should do to enable you to investigate those allegations before we decide whether we should any notice of them?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it is true that none of what the witness started recounting just now can be found in the statement. It is for me extremely important, because the witness can have a lot of problems, too, if it is established in this court that on the 14th of June Mitar Vasiljevic was transferred to the Uzice hospital and he could not have been in Visegrad, as this witness is claiming today, and I hope the Court will be able to establish that. I am particularly surprised by this statement, which she must have known about at the time she gave her previous statement. I personally cannot fathom any reasons why she should not have said that before. And I think it is important, and that I would indeed need time to perhaps prepare, if the witness testifies about these events, for me to prepare for cross-examination at a later stage, as has been suggested by my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, that is a very proper approach to it, but how long do you think that you would need to make some investigation?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not much time, Your Honour, because these are things that I am quite familiar with. So maybe I would need to talk to my client once again, though it is clear to me that the time the witness is referring to is a time that we claim Mitar Vasiljevic could not have been in Visegrad. So maybe already tomorrow I would be ready.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We understand what your case is on this issue very clearly, Mr. Domazet. Very well, then. Well, it may be better then if we leave this witness and to finish tomorrow, reserve the re-examination until tomorrow, and then you and Mr. Domazet can sort out between you what would be the best time to call her tomorrow to finish her evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Would that be suitable, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, quite, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And if you have any particular problems, Mr. Domazet, don't hesitate to raise them, because it is, if I may say so, fairly substantial, the nature of the allegation she's making, quite apart from the time when she says that she saw your client. All right. Well, then, we'll stand that witness down. Can we proceed with your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Just so that the record is complete on such an important issue, I would like to indicate that the statement that we're concerned with was taken on the 20th of January this year, over eight and a half years after the events that the witness was testifying about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, this has been a problem with which this Tribunal is bedevilled, and there are various ways a in which a Tribunal can look at it and it depends on the particular witness, the particular circumstances. Quite often it's the fact that they're being cross-examined that prompts their memory with fresh details. I think that we're all sufficiently experienced in relation to drawing inferences of fact from this sort of thing. There's nothing we can solve in advance, as it were. But it's not just the time in which she says that this happens. It's the nature of the allegations she made, which are quite substantial.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: So we will stand the witness down. Have you got somebody who can explain to her she will be coming back tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The fact that she's already on cross-examination, I would prefer not to talk with her, but if we could just have the VWS people explain to her that that she'll be back tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Perhaps if you could have somebody go to the VWS so they can explain it to her now that she isn't finished but she will be brought back tomorrow. Very well, then. We'll proceed with the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'll defer to my colleague, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Bauer.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Your Honour the Prosecution is calling VG80. The witness sheet will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: 8-0; right?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: 8-0, yes. The witness sheet is pre-numbered 77.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The pseudonym sheet will be Exhibit P77, and it is under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Madam, will you please make the solemn declaration in the document which the usher is showing you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Sit down, please, madam.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Bauer.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Witness VG80, the Court has granted you protective measures in form of a pseudonym called VG80. You will be referred to, throughout the proceedings, as VG80. You will be shown now a piece of paper. Could you please state just yes or no whether it contains your name and date of birth.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG80
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: In 1992, were you married and lived with your two children in the town of Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG80
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Was there a time in spring 1992 when paramilitary formations took over the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG80
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: What kind of paramilitary formations were they, those?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG80
utterances.text: They were the White Eagles, the Seselj people, the Arkan people, and the Serb police.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Were they mostly involved in taking men from their residences?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG80
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: The men that were taken, what kind of ethnicity were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG80
utterances.text: They were predominantly of Muslim ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Were they also involved in searching apartments?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG80
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: What did they search for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG80
utterances.text: They searched for weapons. Their excuse was that they were looking for weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Was your apartment repeatedly searched?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG80
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Were there two occasions where your apartment was searched by two people called Milan Lukic and Sredoje Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG80
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Did you know Milan Lukic from before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG80
utterances.text: I didn't know Milan Lukic before the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Did you know Sredoje Lukic before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG80
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Did you know what he did, where he worked at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG80
utterances.text: I knew that he worked in the Visegrad police, in the SUP.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Did you learn to which group they belonged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG80
utterances.text: I heard they belonged to the White Eagles group, and I only knew that this was a paramilitary formation. I don't know exactly whether they belonged to that paramilitary formation, the White Eagles, for some other paramilitary formation.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Were they armed at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG80
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Did they threaten you in any way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG80
utterances.text: Sredoje Lukic threatened the first time, and the second time it was Milan Lukic. So they alternated.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: What did they say when they threatened you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG80
utterances.text: When they threatened us, they swore at us. They threatened us and made us tell them where the weapons were, where the men were, that the women would be taken away.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Did you have any weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG80
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Was there a night when another soldier from the White Eagles came to your apartment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG80
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: When was this? Sorry, I don't see the answer recorded. It could be that --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We didn't hear her.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Could you please speak up and repeat the answer another time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG80
utterances.text: Where or when did that happen? What was the question?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: When approximately this happened.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG80
utterances.text: It was the end of the month of June.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Was that the night when your husband was taken away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG80
utterances.text: No. They took my husband away on July 2nd.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Thank you. This is the incident I would like to talk to you about. And that night, you said a soldier from the White Eagles came. How did you know it was a soldier from the White Eagles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG80
utterances.text: Well, when he took my husband away, he came back within half an hour and he looked for me. I had left and went to another apartment. He looked for me and found me in that other apartment. That night, first he beat me up, then he raped me, and then he mistreated me. And when I got up in the morning, I realised that he had a badge that had fallen from his uniform. That was a badge belonging to the White Eagle formation.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Was that the next morning that you also decided to leave Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG80
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I looked for my children. I found them. They were separated from me. When I found my children, I decided to leave Visegrad and not wait any longer.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Did you go to Babin Potok that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG80
utterances.text: Yes. I went to Babin Potok from there because my mother lives there.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Were you told that day that it was the 3rd of July 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG80
utterances.text: They Told me when they saw me that it was July 3rd.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: What else did they tell you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG80
utterances.text: They asked me about my husband, where he was, what happened to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Did you ever see your husband again after the events of that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG80
utterances.text: No. I never saw him again.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Did you know the accused, Mitar Vasiljevic, from before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG80
utterances.text: Well, I used to know him because Visegrad is a small place. We used to know each other from sight. We -- well, I didn't have any closer contacts with him. I just knew him from sight.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: How often would you estimate did you see him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG80
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't frequently. Well, accidentally we would meet in town, but I didn't see him especially before the war, only just passing through town I would come across him.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: How did you know it was Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG80
utterances.text: Well, in Visegrad, most people knew one another. It wasn't the case of a big city. It was a small city where we knew one another personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: What did you know was his profession? Sorry, did you know what his profession was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG80
utterances.text: Well, I heard that he was a waiter. I never saw him actually working as a waiter, but I heard that he was employed as a waiter in the catering area.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: How would you describe did he look like at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG80
utterances.text: Well, at the time, well, he was of medium height. He was plumpish. I don't know what else to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: What was his complexion like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG80
utterances.text: He was of a darker complexion, slightly darker complexion. He wasn't of a light complexion.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: And his hair colour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG80
utterances.text: Well, brownish black. He was a dark man.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: What age would you have estimated him at that time? Young, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. middle-aged, old?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG80
utterances.text: Before the war?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Yes, before the war.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG80
utterances.text: Well, he could have been less than 40.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would like to break because we come into another issue which I wouldn't like to interrupt in the middle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: If this is possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think it would be preferable if we continued with this witness in the morning and then went back to the other one. We will have an early mark. We will adjourn now and see you in the morning at 9.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 19th day of September, 2001, at 9.30 a.m.
